Score quantile forecasts against realised values

Source: R/backtest.R
timestral_score.Rd

Scores a timestral_forecast() against the values that were later observed, one row per series, variate and step.

Usage

timestral_score(fc, actual, level = c(80, 98))

Arguments

fc

a timestral_forecast

actual

the realised values over the horizon, shaped like a forecast input with h time steps: a vector or ts (one series, one variate), a matrix with time in rows (one series), a 3-D array (time, variate, series), or a list of those per series

level

interval levels in percent for the coverage columns (fractions in (0, 1) are taken as percentages)

Value

A data frame with columns series, variate, step, actual, median, pinball, crps, ae and one cover<L> column per level.

Details

The scores, for realised value \(y\) and quantile \(q_\tau\) at each level \(\tau\) of the forecast (fc$levels), use the pinball (quantile) loss \(\rho_\tau = (1\{y < q_\tau\} - \tau)(q_\tau - y)\):

  • pinball: \(2\rho_\tau\) averaged over the levels, the quantile loss used in the GluonTS and Chronos benchmarks (before dividing by the scale of the series). The factor 2 makes it equal the absolute error for a point forecast.

  • crps: the continuous ranked probability score, \(2\int_0^1 \rho_\tau\,d\tau\), approximated by the trapezoidal rule over the knots. The knots are not evenly spaced, so they are weighted by their spacing rather than averaged. The integral only covers the knots' range (0.01 to 0.99 for the official checkpoints), so for a point forecast it gives \(0.98|q - y|\) rather than \(|q - y|\): the tails beyond the outermost knots are ignored.

  • ae: the absolute error of the median.

  • cover<L>: whether \(y\) lies in the central L% interval, for each level; each level must pair two knots, as in plot().

Missing actual values give missing scores. Average the rows with stats::aggregate() or dplyr to summarise by step, series or origin.

See also

timestral_backtest() to forecast and score from several origins.

Examples

m <- timestral_load(system.file("extdata", "tiny", package = "timestralR"))
train <- window(AirPassengers, end = c(1959, 12))
test <- window(AirPassengers, start = c(1960, 1))
sc <- timestral_score(timestral_forecast(m, train, h = 12), test)
colMeans(sc[, c("pinball", "crps", "ae", "cover80")])
#>     pinball        crps          ae     cover80 
#> 159.0576796 161.5815572 208.6903368   0.1666667
